A1.justification: Both PDFs describe D-JEPA and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H. Added content can be distinguished reliably from relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet generation and classification experiments, sampling analyses, and audio, video, and multimodal generation results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds JEPA-loss comparisons, ImageNet 512×512 results, and raw-pixel generation evaluations.

M1.justification: The encoders, predictor, EMA updates, prediction and generative losses, and sampling algorithm are unchanged. Raw-pixel operation and flow matching were already described in v1; their additional evaluation does not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: Appendix D.2 adds ImageNet 512×512 conditional generation alongside the existing 256×256 evaluation, extending the required output resolution within the same task. Classification, inpainting, audio, video, and multimodal dataset and task coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds VAR-d16, VAR-d20, and VAR-d24. The new 512×512 comparison also includes previously unevaluated comparators DiffiT and EDM2-XXL. Appendix C.3 uses the existing MAR-B comparator as the baseline without JEPA loss; existing comparison sets are otherwise retained.

E3.justification: The added 512×512 evaluation specifies KL-16 tokenization, a 32×32 token grid, and 480 training epochs. New comparisons evaluate D-JEPA-B checkpoints at 600, 800, and 1400 epochs and generation from raw versus latent inputs. These are targeted protocol extensions; the original experimental setup and sampling searches remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C.3 and Table 6 introduce an explicit JEPA-loss ablation using MAR-B as the control, including an equal-epoch comparison. Table 11 additionally tests how raw-pixel versus latent training affects generation. These substantially extend analysis of central design choices beyond v1's retained sampling, flow-matching, and failure analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and training curves without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added results follow the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results are retained, while substantial entries are added. Table 6 reports 800-epoch D-JEPA-B FID of 3.43 without guidance and 2.01 with guidance. Table 8 reports 512×512 D-JEPA-L FID of 1.89 and 1.62, respectively. Table 11 adds raw-pixel generation scores, and Table 2 adds VAR results. These are additional evaluations, not revisions of the original scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives and updates, Appendix E.1 collapse-prevention argument, and Appendix F flow-matching derivation are retained. No substantive definitions, assumptions, proofs, or mathematical corrections are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of integrating JEPA with generative learning, strong ImageNet performance and scalability, and applicability to continuous and multimodal generation. Terminology clarifications and additional supporting experiments do not materially redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly interprets the MAR-B comparison as evidence for the JEPA loss and earlier convergence. New discussion identifies resource constraints preventing D-JEPA-H evaluation at 512×512 and in raw pixels, while predicting favorable results. The existing VAE interpretation and Appendix H limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 documents the KL-16 tokenizer and token grid for the added resolution, and Table 6 attributes D-JEPA-B's additional 4M parameters to the JEPA-loss MLP. These are limited additions to technical documentation; existing optimizer, hardware, training details, and project access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for classifier-free guidance, VAR, and EDM2. Appendix A reframes the distinction from MAGE around generation across images, audio, and video rather than demonstrated mutual reinforcement between tasks. Additional publication entries for DiffiT and GIVT refer to works already cited in v1.

P1.justification: There are localized introduction and related-work rewrites, new explanatory subsections C.3 and D.2, updated cross-references, and author-affiliation and publication-header edits. The overall narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 6, 8, and 11, expands Table 2, and shortens its caption. Existing appendix tables and figures are reflowed or renumbered. Figures 1–17 retain their plots and image content, and the overall visual design is preserved.

improvement.justification: Table 6 reduces training-budget confounding in v1 by adding an 800-epoch D-JEPA-B comparison with 800-epoch MAR-B, while Tables 8 and 11 substantiate generation at 512×512 and in raw pixels. This strengthens validation of existing claims. The JEPA-loss ablation remains limited to the base model, its unguided FID difference is small (3.43 versus 3.48), and uncertainty estimates are still absent, limiting the strength of the improvement.
